name: P-003 / R-1 live judge-wearer probe on the :3170 current build (identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18)
summary: Two judges were launched through the live :3170 role door (POST /api/agent-mcp/console/bootstrap-role, role judge) on build 3b9df0b66b, whose six P-003 source blobs equal HEAD. One wore a grant-bearing (governed) stack, domain:blueprint-operation-worker (adv_sessions 47811); the other wore a grant-free (ungoverned) stack, ideation:su.mode-ideate (adv_sessions 47812). Each signed judge MCP grant was then exercised at dispatch after the real first-turn path (turn-start-memory, then coord:orient), and the session was ended. All 17 assertions passed and run.sh exited 0. Both judges rendered their worn layer into the prompt. The governed launch recorded role judge with the exact stack and the artifact grants. The ungoverned launch recorded no identity record, by the bootstrap-role.ts contract (it records only grant-bearing artifacts). Neither grant carried superuser, and neither tool list exposed su-only tools. Dispatch refused capability:bash and processes:kill in both runs. The ungoverned judge was refused by the judge role envelope (missing_capability, principal system:judge) and could read plans:get. The governed judge was granted nothing: the papercusp pot (.papercusp/blueprint.yaml fleet.workerRoles) declares capability ceilings for su, operator and researcher but none for judge, so readIdentityGrantPolicy refuses and the grant kernel fails closed with policy-unavailable on every call, the read included. That is no more than its role and pot ceiling.

limitations: The governed judge could not exercise any tool, the in-ceiling read included, because the papercusp pot declares no capability ceiling for the judge role. That satisfies 'granted no more than its role and pot ceiling' but does not show a governed judge receiving a non-empty grant. Declaring a judge ceiling is an administrator pot-policy decision outside P-003, and this run did not make it.

PROBE_GOVERNED is the probe operator's declared expectation for each stack, matching the bootstrap-role.ts recording contract. An earlier probe on the same build (2026-10-20T05:06Z, adv_sessions 47796) first showed that domain:blueprint-operation-worker compiles to a grant-bearing artifact.

Earlier iterations of this probe (2026-10-20T04:58Z-05:08Z, adv_sessions 47785-47797, scratch reports live-judge-probe-1..10) exited 1. Each failed only on an assertion this version replaces: one expected a launch record for the grant-free stack, which the code records by design only for grant-bearing artifacts; the other expected a positive read for the governed judge, which is refused by design without a pot judge ceiling. Two earlier stale-artifact denials (47786/47789) came from the probe skipping the first-turn hook. Its turn-start call is now part of stage 2.
Wearer-authority role selection for host-run identity work (async reactions and the turn-start sink) is covered by the integration tests bound beside this artifact, not by this live run.
